headline: Essential Steamship Authority and Fast Ferry Planning
reservation: Nantucket is an island reachable only by sea or air. Vehicle slots on traditional ferries often sell out six to nine months in advance for the summer season; passenger-only fast ferries are more flexible but still require booking weeks ahead for peak periods. Entry to the island is distinct from securing one of the limited historic inns or seasonal rentals. Always verify current schedules with the official Steamship Authority as high seas or fog can frequently disrupt departures.

days.title: Maritime Roots and Cobblestones

stops.name: Whaling Museum
stops.detail: Explore the island's history as a global whaling capital, featuring a 46-foot sperm whale skeleton and panoramic harbor views from the roof deck.

stops.name: Nantucket Historic District
stops.detail: Walk the uneven cobblestone streets of Main Street to see the 'Three Bricks' mansions and the Oldest House on Sunset Hill.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; primarily a walking day in town
days.note: Wear sturdy shoes for historic cobblestones; avoid thin soles.

days.title: Coastal Moors and Lighthouse Vistas

stops.name: Polpis Path
stops.detail: Cycle this paved route through hidden forests and interior moors toward the eastern shore.

stops.name: Sankaty Head Lighthouse
stops.detail: View the iconic red-and-white striped beacon overlooking the Atlantic and explore the nearby rose-covered cottages of 'Sconset village.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours for cycling; conditions vary with coastal winds
days.note: Check wind direction before heading out; return trips can be strenuous.

days.title: Wild Sands and Wildlife Refuges

stops.name: Sanford Farm and Ram Pasture
stops.detail: Hike through rolling grasslands and former farmland to reach dramatic south shore cliffs.

stops.name: Madaket Beach
stops.detail: Visit the rugged western tip of the island, known for wide sandy expanses and powerful Atlantic surf.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; use local shuttle or bicycles for beach access
days.note: Shorebirds nest seasonally; respect all roped-off conservation areas.

intel.title: Pedestrian Priority
intel.text: The downtown core is best navigated on foot; many streets are narrow one-way lanes not suited for large vehicles. Bicycle rentals are the most efficient way to reach distant beaches without searching for limited car parking.

intel.title: Island Logistics
intel.text: Fuel stations are located near the rotary and airport; prices are significantly higher than the mainland due to transport costs. Ensure vehicles are fueled before exploring the remote western moors.

intel.title: Beach Lot Limits
intel.text: Public lots at Jetties and Surfside are small and frequently reach capacity during summer weekends. Arrive before mid-morning or use the seasonal WAVE shuttle to avoid being turned away.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally strong in town but can become spotty in the interior moors and near Great Point. Download offline maps if planning to hike the Sanford Farm or Polpis trails.

intel.title: The Gray Lady
intel.text: Morning fog is common and can delay flights or ferry crossings; check carrier apps before heading to the terminal. Allow extra travel time if the 'Gray Lady' mist is visible on the horizon.

plan.arrival: Collect luggage at ACK or the ferry terminal; pick up pre-arranged bike rentals and drop bags at your historic inn before a harbor-side lunch.
plan.vehicle: Bicycles are preferred; check ferry restrictions before bringing a mainland car as permit costs are high.
plan.goldenHour: Madaket Beach offers expansive western views; sunsets vary by season and are often enhanced by the 'Gray Lady' fog.
